evidence: Single package ('core') with internal module dependencies (e.g., core.InsertData imported by core.Checks)
No external service communication or network calls — all logic is local and in-process
Clear separation of concerns: Checks, InsertData, User_Functions, Other modules each with distinct responsibilities
Main.py acts as an entry point orchestrating modules, typical of monolithic designs
Low directory depth (2) and small number of packages (1) indicate tight cohesion within a single deployment unit
No ports/adapters or clear separation between core domain and infrastructure (e.g., DB access embedded in core modules)
risks: Tight coupling to database (mysql.connector) in core modules reduces testability and flexibility
Lack of explicit layering (e.g., no domain/service/persistence separation) may hinder maintainability as project scales
No dependency inversion — modules import concrete implementations directly
